A Novel transfer learning based approach for pneumonia detection in chest x-ray images. Applied Sciences, [s.l.], v. | Abstract: | Pneumonia is among the top diseases which cause most of the deaths all over the world. Virus, bacteria and fungi can all cause pneumonia. However, it is difficult to judge the pneumonia just by looking at chest X-rays. The aim of this study is to simplify the pneumonia detection process for experts as well as for novices. We suggest a novel deep learning framework for the detection of pneumonia using the concept of transfer learning. In this approach, features from images are extracted using different neural network models pretrained on ImageNet, which then are fed into a classifier for prediction. We prepared five different models and analyzed their performance. Thereafter, we proposed an ensemble model that combines outputs from all pretrained models, which outperformed individual models, reaching the state-of-the-art performance in pneumonia recognition. Our ensemble model reached an accuracy of 96.4% with a recall of 99.62% on unseen data from the Guangzhou Women and Children’s Medical Center dataset. | Appears in Collections: | DEEL - Artigos publicados em revista científica |. | 2020\_art\_vchouhan.pdf | 4,6 MB | Adobe PDF | View/Open |. Title: A novel ensemble learning framework based on a genetic algorithm for the classification of pneumonia - ScienceDirect
In this study, we propose a novel ensemble CNN framework to accurately detect pneumonia, with optimum weights set by a Genetic Algorithm (GA). Within the realm of medical image analysis, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), a subset of deep learning, are prominently utilized for disease detection (Litjens et al., 2017; Yamashita et al., 2018). Custom CNN models (Liang and Zheng, 2020; Stephen et al., 2019; Rajaraman et al., 2018; Saraiva et al., 2019), transfer learning (Jain et al., 2020; Salehi et al., 2021; Latif et al., 2021; Kermany et al., 2018; Moujahid et al., 2020; Ayan and Ünver, 2019), and ensemble learning (Chouhan et al., 2020; Vrbancic and Podgorelec, 2022; Hashmi et al., 2020; Livieris et al., 2019; Mabrouk et al., 2022) approaches are used to detect pneumonia from chest X-rays. In this study, an extensive experimental study has been carried out to establish the performance of CNN models at various noise levels in chest X-ray images (Kermany, et al.; Kermany et al., 2018), as well as their behavior under varied transfer learning circumstances and in imbalanced dataset situations. Since the ensemble learning approach can combine the benefits of multiple models, the proposed framework for pneumonia detection was thoroughly optimized. In the ensemble learning method, we have reached the optimum result that will minimize the loss and maximize the accuracy values of each model with the real-valued Genetic Algorithm (GA) (Haupt and Haupt, 2004; Kaya et al., 2021b) for the problem of which weights the models will contribute to the result. The reason for this work, however, was the lack of determining the best base CNN models and their weights to the ensemble learning method to detect pneumonia accurately. Custom CNN models, transfer of the weight of the existing models trained on the ImageNet and ensemble learning techniques were utilized to diagnose pneumonia on X-ray pictures. ### Pneumonia detection in chest X-ray images using convolutional neural networks and transfer learning. ### A novel transfer learning based approach for pneumonia detection in chest X-ray images. This study proposes a deep learning model for automatic OA classification from X-ray images, optimized using a Genetic Algorithm (GA) to enhance performance.

# Transfer Learning Based Approach for Pneumonia Detection Using Customized VGG16 Deep Learning Model. Pneumonia is normally detected by a highly-trained consultant’s examination of a chest X-Ray radiograph. To address this, we develop a deep learning-based approach using a complex Visual Group Geometry VGG16 model to detect the presence of pneumonia. The proposed model has been trained on a collection of 5856 chest X-Ray images (4273 scans of pneumonia class and 1583 scans of normal class). ### Early Detection and Prediction of Pneumonia Disease Using VGG16 Deep Learning Technique. ### A Deep Learning Model for Early Prediction of Pneumonia Using VGG19 and Neural Networks. results.title: Pediatric pneumonia diagnosis using stacked ensemble learning on multi-model deep CNN architectures | Multimedia Tools and Applications | Springer Nature Link
results.content:
Title: Pediatric pneumonia diagnosis using stacked ensemble learning on multi-model deep CNN architectures | Multimedia Tools and Applications | Springer Nature Link
# Pediatric pneumonia diagnosis using stacked ensemble learning on multi-model deep CNN architectures. Being non-invasive and painless, chest X-rays are the most common modality for pediatric pneumonia diagnosis. This challenge initiates the need for an unerring computer-aided diagnosis model. Our work proposes Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization for image enhancement and a stacking classifier based on the fusion of deep learning-based features for pediatric pneumonia diagnosis. The extracted features from the global average pooling layers of the fine-tuned MobileNet, DenseNet121, DenseNet169, and DenseNet201 are concatenated for the final classification using a stacked ensemble classifier. We expect this model to greatly help the real-time diagnosis of pediatric pneumonia. ### Stacked ensemble learning based on deep convolutional neural networks for pediatric pneumonia diagnosis using chest X-ray images. ### Transfer Learning Based Pediatric Pneumonia Diagnosis Using Residual Attention Learning. ### Prediction of Pediatric Pneumonia Based on Stacked Ensemble Methods in Deep Learning.
